In this module, we have seen:

- how to create a local Git repository, make commits, and create and navigate branches (exercise 1)
- how to interact with a Git repository stored on GitHub (exercise 2)
- how to use the "fork and pull" model to collaborate on another person's GitHub repository (exercise 3)

Becoming familiar with all these concepts takes time, but you are now armed to start contributing to any GitHub repository! Contributing code or documentation to open-source projects can take many forms. To become more comfortable with this process, you can start by suggesting simple patches to the documentation of an open-source project, and then gradually increase the difficulty of your contributions. 

Note that collaborating on GitHub goes beyond the technical skills to handle version control tools. As a follow-up you might be interested in our module on ["Code review"](https://palaeoverse.org/modules/pr-preview/pr-40/training/modules-dev/code_review/index.html).
